Rashi on Shabbat 41a:10:1.hebrew: מאי קאמר - מאי פינהו? ומאי לא יתן — והדר אמר אבל נותן:
Rashi on Shabbat 41a:10:1.english: What is [the Mishnah] saying? - What is [the meaning of] "he cleared it"? And what is [the meaning of] "he shall not put," yet then it states "however, he may put"?

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:1:1.hebrew: דלית ליה גידודי - שאין שפתה גבוהה שיהיו המים עמוקים אצל שפתה כמו באמצע. דכיון שאין עמוקים שם, כי מטי סמוך לשפתה נועץ רגליו בקרקע וחופר, וממחה העפר לתוך המים, ודמי למגבל. ולי נראה: דאית ליה גידודי שרי, דלא דמי לנהר אלא לכלי; דלית ליה גידודי — דמיא לנהר, ואסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 41a:1:1.english: That does not have embankments - [This means] that its rim is not high [such] that the water would be deep near its edge as in the middle. For since [the water] is not deep there, when he arrives close to its edge, he sticks his feet into the ground and digs, and dissolves the dirt into the water, which resembles kneading. And it seems to me: [A pool] that has embankments is permitted, because it does not resemble a river but rather a vessel; [whereas one] that does not have embankments resembles a river, and [is therefore] forbidden.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:2:1.english: That he placed his hands - When he was bathing, for the sake of modesty.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:2:3.hebrew: כאילו מביא מבול לעולם - שמתחמם ובא לידי קרי, וזה קלקולו של דור המבול — מוציאים שכבת זרע לבטלה, דכתיב: "כי השחית כל בשר" וגו' (בראשית ו׳:י״ב):
Rashi on Shabbat 41a:2:3.english: As if he brings a flood to the world - For he becomes aroused and comes to [have] a seminal emission, and this was the corruption of the generation of the Flood — [that they were] emitting semen in vain, as it is written: “For all flesh had corrupted...” (Genesis 6:12).

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:3:1.hebrew: כבולשת - עשאוה להא דר' אבוה בולשת — חיילות, גייס הבא לעיר. על שם שמחפשין ובולשים את העיר, קרי לה בולשת:
Rashi on Shabbat 41a:3:1.english: Like a military unit - They treated this [matter] of Rabbi Abbahu as a military unit [boleshet] — troops, an invading force that comes to the city. Because they search and scour the city, it is called a boleshet.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:3:2.english: During peacetime - For example, when it belongs to that [same] kingdom:

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:4:1.english: As if he denies - For it appears that he is ashamed of the matter [of circumcision].

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:4:2.hebrew: כי נחית - לנהר, פניו כלפי הנהר, ואין כאן משום צניעות — אסור לכסותו:
Rashi on Shabbat 41a:4:2.english: When he descends - Into the river, his face is toward the river, and there is no [concern] of modesty here — it is forbidden to cover it.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:4:3.hebrew: כי סליק - ופניו כלפי העם, מותר משום צניעות:
Rashi on Shabbat 41a:4:3.english: When he emerges - and his face is toward the people, [covering himself] is permitted on account of modesty.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:4:4.hebrew: ר' זירא זקיף - דחייש לדרב, שלא יראה ככופר:
Rashi on Shabbat 41a:4:4.english: Rabbi Zeira stood upright - For he was concerned about [the statement of] Rav, so that he would not appear like one who denies [the covenant].

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:5:1.hebrew: משתמיט - היה ירא ליראות לו, משום דהוה בעי רבי זירא למיסק לארעא דישראל, ורב יהודה לא סבירא ליה, וירא פן יגזור עליו מלילך:
Rashi on Shabbat 41a:5:1.english: Was avoiding - He was afraid to appear before him, because Rabbi Zeira wanted to ascend to the Land of Israel and Rav Yehuda did not hold [of this], and [Rabbi Zeira] was afraid lest [Rav Yehuda] decree upon him not to go.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:5:2.hebrew: בבלה יובאו ושמה יהיו עד יום פקדי וגו' - ור' זירא אמר לך: האי קרא בכלי שרת כתיב, כדאמרינן בשני דייני גזירות (כתובות קיא.):
Rashi on Shabbat 41a:5:2.english: They shall be taken to Babylonia and there they shall remain until the day that I recall them, etc. - And Rabbi Zeira [would] say to you: This verse is written concerning the service vessels [of the Temple], as we say in the chapter [entitled] Shnei Dayyanei Gezerot (Ketubot 111a).

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:5:3.hebrew: הביאו לי נתר - לחוף את ראשי, וקאמר להו בלשון הקודש:
Rashi on Shabbat 41a:5:3.english: Bring me natron - [In order] to wash my head; and he said [this] to them in the Holy Tongue.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:5:4.hebrew: פתחו פומייכו - ויכנס הבל בית המרחץ לתוך הגוף, ויוציא הבל של זיעה:
Rashi on Shabbat 41a:5:4.english: Open your mouths - [So that] the steam of the bathhouse will enter into the body, and expel the vapor of perspiration.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:5:5.hebrew: ואשתו - מן מים חמין, ואפי' לא הוחמו אלא לרחיצה:
Rashi on Shabbat 41a:5:5.english: And drink - From the hot water, even if it was heated only for bathing.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:6:1.hebrew: מותר לאומרן - בבית המרחץ, ואפי' בלשון קודש:
Rashi on Shabbat 41a:6:1.english: [It is] permitted to say them - In the bathhouse, and even in the Holy Tongue.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:6:10.hebrew: למים ע"ג חבית - על שוליו וצדדיו, שאינם נכנסים לתוכו:
Rashi on Shabbat 41a:6:10.english: [Similar] to water on top of a barrel - On its bottom and its sides, which do not enter into it.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:6:2.english: Heat - That of the bathhouse, which enters through the mouth.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:6:3.english: Brings out heat - [The heat] of perspiration.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:6:4.hebrew: ולא הלך ד' אמות - קודם שישן:
Rashi on Shabbat 41a:6:4.english: And did not walk four cubits - Before going to sleep.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:6:5.english: Rots - It is not digested to become waste.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:6:6.english: Bad odor - Odor of the mouth.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:6:7.english: Odor of filth - His entire body is constantly foul with sweat.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:6:8.english: And did not heat it from the inside - Which does not do any good at all.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:6:9.english: And did not place it in cold [water] - For [cold water] strengthens the iron.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:7:1.hebrew: מוליאר הגרוף - מן הגחלים מבע"י:
Rashi on Shabbat 41a:7:1.english: A swept mulyar - [Swept] of the coals while it was still day.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:7:2.hebrew: שותין - ממימיו בשבת, ואע"פ שהוחמו קצת מחמת הכלי, לפי שאינו מוסיף הבל אלא משמר ומקיים חום שלהם שלא יצטננו. בגמרא מפרש: מוליאר — מים מבפנים וגחלים מבחוץ — כלי שיש בו בית קיבול קטן אצל דופנו מבחוץ מחובר לו, ונותן שם גחלים, והמים בקיבולו הגדול. ורבותינו מפרשים: מוליאר — שני שולים, ואנטיכי — בי דודי, מחיצה בינתיים. ולי נראה להפך: דאם כן, ה"ל למיתני מים מלמעלה וגחלים מלמטה. ועוד, דנחשתה דתני באנטיכי — לשון שולים הן, והן אומרים: לשון נחושת, ושאני נחשת מחרס:
Rashi on Shabbat 41a:7:2.english: One may drink - From its water on Shabbat; and even though it was heated a little on account of the vessel, [this is permitted] because [the vessel] does not add heat, but rather preserves and maintains its heat so that it does not cool down. In the Gemara, [it] explains: "A mulyar [has] water on the inside and coals on the outside" — a vessel that has a small receptacle attached to it on the outside along its wall, and one places coals there, while the water is in its large receptacle. And our Rabbis explain: A mulyar [has] two bottoms, and an antikhi is bei dodei [two pots], [with] a partition between them. But to me it seems the opposite: for if so, it should have taught "water on top and coals on the bottom"; and furthermore, neḥushtah, which is taught regarding an antikhi, is an expression of "bottom," whereas they say [it is] an expression of copper, and that copper is different from earthenware.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:7:3.english: An antikhi - [This is] explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:8:1.hebrew: בי כירי - חלל יש בכירה אצל חלליה שהגחלים בו, ומים נתונים בחללה השני. ואע"ג דדמי למוליאר, מיהו כירה דופנה עב, והאור תדיר בתוכה כל ימות החול, ודופנה חם מאד, ומוסיף הבל במים, אע"פ שגרופה מן הגחלים:
Rashi on Shabbat 41a:8:1.english: A stove compartment - There is a cavity in a stove next to its cavity in which the coals are [placed], and water is placed in its second cavity. And even though it is similar to a mulyar, nevertheless, the wall of a stove is thick, and fire is constantly inside it throughout the weekdays, and its wall is very hot and adds heat to the water, even though it was swept of the coals.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:8:2.hebrew: בי דודי - יורה גדולה. עושין לה שתי שוליים, ונותנין גחלים בין שניהם, והמים על העליונים:
Rashi on Shabbat 41a:8:2.english: A place of cauldrons - A large cauldron: they make two bottoms for it, and place coals between the two of them, and the water is on the upper [bottom].

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:8:3.hebrew: וכל שכן - דבי כירי אסור, כדפרישית, שמתוך שהאור תדיר בו ודופנו עב, מרתיח:
Rashi on Shabbat 41a:8:3.english: All the more so - That [the cavity of] a stove is forbidden, as I explained, since fire is constantly within it and its wall is thick, it boils [the water].

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:8:4.english: But [regarding] a bei dudei, no - For it is like a mulyar.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:8:5.hebrew: שנחושתה - נחושת שלה; אלמא ביורה של נחשת קאי, ונחשת משמר רתיחתו. ואני אומר: נחושתה — לשון שולים, כדכתיב (יחזקאל ט״ז:ל״ו): "יען השפך נחשתך", ולשון של המשנה: "נחשתו של תנור" במסכת כלים (פ"ח מ"ג). ושאני אנטיכי ממוליאר, דמתוך שהשולים מכוסים — חומם משתמר, ואע"ג שגרפו גחליהם:
Rashi on Shabbat 41a:8:5.english: Because its copper - [That is,] its copper [metal]. Consequently, [the baraita] is dealing with a cauldron of copper, and copper retains its boiling heat. But I say: Nechoshtah is an expression for the bottom, as it is written (Ezekiel 16:36): “Because your bottom was poured out,” and the phrasing of the Mishnah: “the bottom of an oven” in Tractate Kelim (8:3). And an antikhi is different from a mulyar, for since the bottom is covered, its heat is retained, even though they swept their coals.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:9:1.english: The urn - A kettle for hot water.

Rashi on Shabbat 41a:9:2.english: That was emptied - The entire Mishnah is explained in the Gemara.

Tosafot on Shabbat 41a:2:1.hebrew: פשיטא דלא נגע דתניא ר' אליעזר אומר כו' - ואע"ג דרבנן פליגי עליה ושרו בפרק כל היד (נדה יג. ושם), לא שרי אלא משום ממזרות — שלא יראה ככרות שפכה, ויוציאו לעז על בניו שהן ממזרים:
Tosafot on Shabbat 41a:2:1.english: "It is obvious that he did not touch, as it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says, etc." - And even though the Rabbis disagree with him and permit [it] in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaYad (Niddah 13a and ibid.), they only permitted [it] due to [concern over] illegitimacy [mamzerut] — so that he does not appear as one whose penis is severed [kerut shofkhah], and [people] will cast aspersions on his children that they are mamzerim [illegitimate].

Tosafot on Shabbat 41a:6:1.hebrew: רחץ ולא סך - ול"ג "מעיקרא", דהא בכולי הש"ס רחיצה קודם סיכה, כדאמר בפ"ק דקידושין (דף כב:): "רחצו, סכו", וקרא כתיב: "ורחצת וסכת" (רות נ). מיהו קרא איכא לאוקמי בסיכה שהיתה מתקשטת עצמה לריח טוב; לכן לא היתה סכה בתחלה, שעל ידי רחיצה היתה מעברת הסיכה מעליה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 41a:6:1.english: "Bathed and did not anoint" - And we do not read "initially," for throughout the entire Talmud, washing precedes anointing, as [the Gemara] says in the first chapter of Kiddushin (22b): "[If he] washed him, anointed him," and Scripture writes: "Wash yourself and anoint yourself" (Ruth 3:3). However, the verse can be established [as referring to] anointing where she was adorning herself for a pleasant fragrance; therefore she would not anoint initially, since by means of washing she would remove the ointment from upon herself.

Tosafot on Shabbat 41a:7:1.hebrew: מוליאר הגרוף שותין ממנו בשבת - פי' בקונטרס: לפי שאין מוסיף הבל, אלא משמר ומקיים חום שלהן; ואנטיכי, אפי' גרופה, אין שותין הימנה, לפי שמוספת הבל. ואין נראה, דלא שייך למיגזר במוסיף הבל אלא בהטמנה, גזירה שמא יטמין ברמץ. ועוד, דדוחק לומר דמתני' איירי כשעשה האיסור. ועוד, דאכטיכי אוסר בכל ענין לשתות הימנו, אפילו בהשהאה; ואי להחזיר תנן, משהין אפילו באינו גרוף! ועוד, אי משום תוספת הבל אסרה ליה מתני' בשתיה, תקשה לרבה ורב יוסף, דשרו לעיל (שבת דף לח.) בשכח קדרה ע"ג כירה ובשלה בשבת, אע"ג דלא נתבשלה כמאכל בן דרוסאי, ואפי' במזיד. ונראה כפי' ה"ר פורת: מוליאר הגרוף שותין הימנו בשבת — שמוזגין המים חמין ביין, לפי שהמים אינן כ"כ חמין במוליאר שיתבשל היין מן המים שמוזגין לתוכו; אבל אנטיכי, אע"פ שגרופה, אין שותין הימנה — לפי שאנטיכי יש בה הבל יותר, ומתבשל היין מן המים בשעת מזיגה. וכ"מ בירושלמי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 41a:7:1.english: One may drink from a swept mulyar on Shabbat — Rashi explained: Because it does not add heat, but rather preserves and maintains their heat; while [with regard to] an antikhi, even if swept, one may not drink from it because it adds heat. And this does not appear [correct], for it is not relevant to issue a decree regarding [something that] adds heat except in [the case of] insulation [hatmanah], as a decree lest one insulate in hot ashes. And furthermore, it is difficult to say that the Mishnah is dealing with [a case where] one committed the transgression. And furthermore, [the Mishnah] forbids drinking from an antikhi in all circumstances, even in [a case of merely] leaving [it from before Shabbat]; and if we learn [the earlier Mishnah as referring to] returning [a pot to the stove, then] one may leave [it] even on [a stove that is] not swept! And furthermore, if the Mishnah prohibited drinking from it due to the addition of heat, this would pose a difficulty for Rabba and Rav Yosef, who permitted above (Shabbat 38a) [food in a case where] one forgot a pot on a stove and it cooked on Shabbat, even though it had not [yet] been cooked to the extent of the food of Ben Derusai [before Shabbat], and even [if he left it there] intentionally! And the explanation of Rabbeinu Porat appears [correct]: "One may drink from a swept mulyar on Shabbat" — [this means] that one may dilute wine with the hot water, because the water is not so hot in a mulyar that the wine would be cooked by the water poured into it; but [with regard to] an antikhi, even if swept, one may not drink from it, because an antikhi retains more heat, and the wine is cooked by the water at the time of dilution. And so it is implied in the Yerushalmi.
